wiki_text: On 27 January 2026, Greece's Ministry of Environment and Energy signed the environmental permit for the Thrace FSRU, a second floating LNG import terminal proposed by Gastrade in the same Aegean sea area as the operating Alexandroupolis FSRU. The project capacity was revised to 6 bcm/year (about 4.4 mtpa). A final investment decision remained pending the resolution of financing (estimated cost at least EUR650 million, with no European Investment Bank subsidy or preferential financing available), and potential operations were cited for 2028.

Regasification at the Alexandroupolis FSRU was suspended in late January 2025 after a technical issue damaged the booster pumps aboard the FSRU. Gastrade restarted operations in August 2025 at a reduced regasification capacity (45.4 GWh/day), then increased the maximum capacity to 90.8 GWh/day (12 September 2025) and 136.2 GWh/day (21 October 2025). TotalEnergies and Metlen Energy & Metals were selected to supply LNG for October and December 2025, with Metlen and Shell supplying January and March 2026.
